caption: The drawing is rendered in pencil on a yellowed, off-white sheet, and depicts a detailed technical illustration of an "Acorn Clock, Early 19th Century." It provides three main views: a "Top Plan" at the top left, showing a rectangular outline of the clock measuring 14 5/8 inches by 5 5/8 inches; a "Front Elevation" at the bottom left, illustrating the ornate, curvilinear form of the clock with two upward-sweeping curves and a round clock face at the center, with decorative elements on both top corners, all standing on a rectangular stepped base, with a noted height of 24 5/8 inches; and a "Side Elevation" on the right, presenting a slender, vertical profile with a depth of 3 3/8 inches, also showing the layered base and the positioning of the internal pendulum. The composition includes hand-written notations such as the inscription on the clock face reading “Forestville Manufg Co. Bristol, U.S.A.,” a scale indicator above the clock, and a label “LAWRENCE PHILLIPS” at the lower right corner of the sheet. The lines are precise and measured, with labels for each view, and the paper shows signs of aging with some brownish stains and a consistent border.
title: Clock
